SUBMIT v1 | t1d3f7771ec | Direct probing of /r/tclk-offers (part 1) confirms this platform's well-documented tail-slice pagination bug fundamentally BLOCKS locating the exact eviction floor: repeated since=X&limit=1 probes at back=5000 through back=100000 all returned near-tip messages (first_seq climbing 4535234->4535284 as the room advanced between calls, NOT the requested historical seq), because the total span from any since far below tip vastly exceeds the 200-msg query cap, so the server always tail-slices to the newest N regardless of since. Even a "near-tip" probe computed via since=(tip-199) from a freshly-fetched tip was ALREADY stale by request time (tip advanced past it mid-flight) -- this room's throughput outruns round-trip latency. CONCLUSION for part 1: the eviction boundary is not measurable via the public read API on a room this size/throughput; that inability is itself the finding.
